title: A US Water Main Breaks About Every 2 Minutes #shorts
summary: The US has about 240,000 water main breaks a year (ASCE 2025), roughly one every two minutes (our math), across more than 2 million miles of pipe, and 9.2 million lead service lines are still in use.
sources: Roughly half of US surface-water drinking water plants serving more than 10,000 people are affected by at least one upstream treated wastewater discharge; modeled de facto reuse at 25 plants ranged from <0.1 to 13% of intake at average flow and >80% at low flow, highest 84% at one plant (Nguyen et al., Journal AWWA 110(4), 2018, modeled): https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10079854

De facto water reuse: a drinking water supply that contains a significant fraction of wastewater effluent; common across the US (US EPA research grant page): https://www.epa.gov/research-grants/national-priorities-occurrence-and-implications-de-facto-water-reuse-drinking-water

Public supply withdrew about 35,823 million gallons per day in the lower 48 in 2020: 18,586 Mgal/d (about 52%) surface water, 17,236 Mgal/d (about 48%) groundwater (USGS, modeled estimates): https://www.usgs.gov/mission-areas/water-resources/science/public-supply-water-use

Community water treatment steps: coagulation, flocculation, sedimentation, filtration (sand, gravel, charcoal), disinfection (CDC, How Water Treatment Works): https://www.cdc.gov/drinking-water/about/how-water-treatment-works.html

More than 2 million miles of drinking water pipe; approximately 240,000 water main breaks per year; 9.2 million lead service lines in operation (EPA 2023 figure) (ASCE 2025 Infrastructure Report Card, Drinking Water): https://infrastructurereportcard.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Drinking-Water.pdf

Over 148,000 public water systems in the US provide drinking water to 90 percent of Americans (US EPA, Information about Public Water Systems): https://19january2025snapshot.epa.gov/dwreginfo/information-about-public-water-systems
One break about every 2 minutes: 525,600 minutes in a year / 240,000 breaks = about 2.2 minutes (our math from the ASCE figure).

About 80 times around the Earth: 2,000,000 miles / about 24,901 miles around the equator (2 x pi x the 6,378 km equatorial radius in the NASA Earth fact sheet: https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/earthfact.html) = about 80 (our math).

scenes.narration: A US water main breaks about every two minutes.
That's about {240,000|two hundred forty thousand} breaks a year.
Spread across more than {2 million|two million} miles of pipe under our streets. That's enough to circle the Earth about {80|eighty} times.
And {9.2 million|nine point two million} lead service lines are still in use, carrying water into homes and buildings.
